syllabus.head: Water Chemistry
syllabus.text: Hardness of water (types: temporary/carbonate and permanent/non-carbonate; causes, units, and boiler troubles: scale, sludge, priming, foaming, caustic embrittlement).

Water softening processes: External treatments including Clark's process, Lime-Soda process (cold and hot), Zeolite (Permutit) process, Ion-Exchange (Demineralization) resin process, Reverse Osmosis (RO), and internal treatments (Calgon, phosphate, carbonate conditioning).
Alkalinity of water: Causes, determination, chemical reactions, and EDTA complexometric titration.

syllabus.head: Corrosion Chemistry
syllabus.text: Theories of corrosion (Dry/Chemical vs. Wet/Electrochemical corrosion).
Mechanisms of electrochemical corrosion: Hydrogen evolution and oxygen absorption mechanisms (rusting of iron).
Types of corrosion: Galvanic, differential aeration, pitting, stress corrosion.
Factors affecting rate of corrosion: Environmental and metallurgical factors.

Corrosion control methods: Material selection, cathodic protection (sacrificial anode vs. impressed current cathodic protection), and protective surface coatings (galvanizing, tinning, noble vs. sacrificial coatings).

syllabus.head: Polymers & Macromolecules
syllabus.text: Classification of polymers (origin, structure, molecular forces, tacticity: isotactic, syndiotactic, atactic).
Polymerization mechanisms: Addition (chain-growth) vs. Condensation (step-growth) polymerization, free-radical mechanism, functionality of monomers.

Industrial plastics, resins, and elastomers: Preparation, properties, and applications of PVC, PMMA, PAN, PET, Polyamides (Nylon-6, Nylon-6,6), Polyurethane, Polyethylene, Polypropylene, Teflon (PTFE), and synthetic rubbers (Buna-S, Buna-N).
Advanced functional polymers: Conducting polymers (mechanism, classification, doping, and conductivity enhancement) and biodegradable polymers.
Rubber: Natural rubber processing and vulcanization of rubber (sulfur cross-linking mechanism, mechanical properties, and structural improvements).

syllabus.head: Glass
syllabus.text: Toughened glass, laminated safety glass, raw materials, and strengthening processes of glass.

syllabus.head: Fuels & Combustion
syllabus.text: Gross Calorific Value (GCV) and Net Calorific Value (NCV), determination of calorific value using Bomb Calorimeter (corrections: fuse wire, acid, cooling, cotton thread).
Alternative energy sources: Biomass, Biogas production stages (hydrolysis, acidogenesis, methanogenesis), and Biofuels.
Environment and air pollution: Causes, effects, and greenhouse gases.

syllabus.head: Lubricants
syllabus.text: Classification of lubricants (liquid, semi-solid, solid lubricants), mechanisms of lubrication (fluid film/hydrodynamic, thin film/boundary, and extreme pressure lubrication).
Lubricant properties and testing: Flash point, Fire point, Pour point, Cloud point, Aniline point, and Viscosity Index (definition, determination, and calculation).

labs.title: Polymerization & Lubrication Regimes Simulator
points: Physical 3D Assets:
Macro Mode: Journal bearing shaft rotating within a sleeve casing separated by a lubricating oil film.
Micro Mode: Polymer chain network showing cross-linking under sulfur vulcanization and electron delocalization along conjugated polyacetylene backbones.
Interactive Controls:
Lubrication load force slider (100 N to 10,000 N) and shaft rotation speed (RPM).
Oil temperature slider (0°C to 150°C) to observe viscosity changes based on Viscosity Index.
Polymer dopant slider (I<sub>2</sub> vapor dopant concentration for polyacetylene).
Real-Time Visual Mechanics:
Dynamically demonstrates the Stribeck Curve transitions: Fluid film (surfaces completely separated) → Mixed → Boundary lubrication (asperity metal-to-metal contact).
Microscopic polymer mode shows generation of positive polarons/solitons along carbon chains upon doping, increasing electrical conductivity by multiple orders of magnitude.

units.title: Spectroscopic Techniques, Organic Reactions & Drug Synthesis

syllabus.head: Spectroscopy
syllabus.text: Principles of spectroscopy, electromagnetic radiation spectrum, selection rules, Born-Oppenheimer approximation.

syllabus.head: Electronic (UV-Visible) Spectroscopy
syllabus.text: Types of electronic transitions (σ → σ, n → σ, π → π, n → π), chromophores, auxochromes, absorption shifts (bathochromic, hypsochromic, hyperchromic, hypochromic), Beer-Lambert Law and applications.

syllabus.head: Vibrational (IR) Spectroscopy
syllabus.text: Principle, molecular vibrations (stretching: symmetric/asymmetric; bending: scissoring, rocking, wagging, twisting), selection rule (dμ/dx ≠ 0), calculation of vibrational degrees of freedom (3N-6 and 3N-5), and importance of the fingerprint region.

syllabus.head: Rotational (Microwave) Spectroscopy
syllabus.text: Rigid rotor model, selection rule (ΔJ = ±1), determination of bond lengths.

syllabus.head: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (1H NMR) Spectroscopy & MRI
syllabus.text: Principle, nuclear spin states, chemical shift (δ scale), shielding and deshielding mechanisms, spin-spin coupling and coupling constant, TMS as internal reference, structure elucidation of organic molecules, basic principle of Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI).

syllabus.head: Basic Organic Reaction Mechanisms
syllabus.text: Addition reactions (electrophilic and nucleophilic addition), Substitution reactions (S<sub>N</sub>1 and S<sub>N</sub>2 mechanisms with kinetics and stereochemistry: Walden inversion vs. racemization), Elimination reactions, Cyclization reactions (Diels-Alder [4+2] cycloaddition).

syllabus.head: Drug Synthesis
syllabus.text: Complete synthesis pathways, reaction conditions, and pharmaceutical uses of: Aspirin, Phenacetin, Melubrin, or Novalgin.

labs.title: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (1H NMR) & MRI Spectrometer
points: Physical 3D Assets:
Superconducting cryo-magnet dewar with liquid helium/nitrogen ports, radiofrequency (RF) transmitter coil, receiver detection coil, spinning 5mm NMR sample tube assembly, and spectrum workstation.
Interactive Controls:
Molecular sample library: Isobutyl bromide (C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>9</sub>Br), tert-Butylbenzene vs. Isobutylbenzene (C<sub>10</sub>H<sub>14</sub>), Ethanol (CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>OH).
External magnetic field strength B<sub>0</sub> slider (1.4 T [60 MHz] to 14.1 T [600 MHz]).
RF pulse frequency sweep control.
Real-Time Visual Mechanics:
Shows nuclear Zeeman splitting of proton magnetic moments into parallel (α-spin, m<sub>I</sub> = +1/2) and anti-parallel (β-spin, m<sub>I</sub> = -1/2) states.
Resonance condition occurs when hν= γħB<sub>0</sub>(1 - σ); flips spin states and generates an induction signal (FID).

Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) displays the real-time spectrum: Shows TMS reference peak at δ= 0 ppm, chemical shifts based on electron-withdrawing inductive shielding/deshielding, and multi-peak spin-spin splitting adhering strictly to Pascal's triangle (n+1 rule).

labs.title: Organic Reaction Mechanisms & Molecular Collision Visualizer
points: Physical 3D Assets:
Dynamic 3D ball-and-stick / space-filling molecular models of organic reactants, nucleophiles, and leaving groups.
Synchronized Reaction Coordinate Energy Diagram (ΔG<sup>‡</sup> vs. Reaction Progress).
Interactive Controls:
Reaction mechanism selector: S<sub>N</sub>1 (2-step tertiary halide) vs. S<sub>N</sub>2 (1-step primary halide) vs. Diels-Alder [4+2] cycloaddition.
Substrate steric hindrance slider: Primary (1°) → Secondary (2°) → Tertiary (3°) alkyl halides.
Nucleophile strength and solvent polarity (Polar protic vs. Polar aprotic) toggles.
Real-Time Visual Mechanics:

S<sub>N</sub>2 Path: Visualizes backside nucleophilic attack at 180° to the leaving group, formation of the planar pentacoordinate transition state [Nu⋯C ⋯X]<sup>‡</sup>, and umbrella-like Walden inversion of stereochemical configuration.

S<sub>N</sub>1 Path: Shows heterolytic cleavage of the leaving group forming a planar sp<sup>2</sup> hybridized carbocation intermediate, followed by equal probability nucleophilic attack from top and bottom faces, producing a racemic (±) mixture.
